summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by dependence on gastrostomy tube feeds for post-bypass hypoglycemia and a history of marginal ulcers was admitted to the surgery service for worsening abdominal pain that had shifted from chronic G-tube site discomfort to epigastric/right upper quadrant pain similar to prior ulcer episodes, with some leakage around the tube but no vomiting or bleeding. She was treated with bowel rest, IV fluids, and IV pantoprazole; right upper quadrant ultrasound showed no cholelithiasis or cholecystitis, and she remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable. With continued IV acid suppression and addition of sucralfate, her pain improved significantly, and she tolerated enteral tube feeds and water by mouth. She was discharged home ambulatory with instructions for water by mouth only, NutriHep tube feeds at 50 mL/hr continuously, ongoing PPI therapy plus sucralfate, avoidance of NSAIDs/alcohol/tobacco, monitoring of the G-tube site, and follow-up with her surgeon for scheduled G-tube revisional surgery.
